# Scenario reference

<!-- Generated by `synthiq-caller reference --out docs/SCENARIO-REFERENCE.md`. Do not edit by hand: change `scenario.py` or `reference.py` and regenerate. A test fails when this page is out of date. -->

A scenario is one JSON file (YAML too, when PyYAML is installed). It says who is calling, what they say to which question, and what must be true after. Nothing in it knows about any voice engine. A file with a `chain` key is a chain of calls, described in `RESET-READ-BACK-CHAINS.md`; a target profile is described in `TARGETS-REHEARSAL-AND-SAFETY.md`.

A scenario that states no expectation (no `expect.tools`, `fields`, `agent_says`, `agent_never_says`, `read_back` or booking part) is ungradeable: a call is never passed for having happened.

## A complete small scenario

```json
{
  "name": "caller gives a date of birth",
  "mutates": "none",
  "persona": {
    "facts": {
      "date_of_birth": "2000-01-01"
    }
  },
  "steps": [
    {
      "when": "how can i help",
      "clips": [
        "opener"
      ],
      "intended": "I have a question."
    },
    {
      "when": "date of birth",
      "clips": [
        "dob"
      ],
      "field": "date_of_birth"
    }
  ],
  "hangup_after": "goodbye",
  "max_seconds": 90,
  "expect": {
    "tools": [
      {
        "name_contains": "lookup"
      }
    ],
    "fields": [
      "date_of_birth"
    ],
    "agent_says": [
      "thank you"
    ]
  }
}
```

## Allowed values

- Persona fact names (and `field` on a step): `name`, `date_of_birth`, `postcode`, `phone`
- `mutates`, least to most: `none`, `registers`, `books`, `moves`, `unknown`. `unknown` is the default and is treated as the most dangerous
- A scenario at these `mutates` levels must state `expect.booking`: `books`, `moves`
- `expect.booking.weekdays`: `monday`, `tuesday`, `wednesday`, `thursday`, `friday`, `saturday`, `sunday`
- A batch's `--allow-mutating` (and a target profile's `allow_mutating`), least to most: `none`, `registers`, `books`, `all`

## Scenario

The top level of a scenario file.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | text | required | A name for the scenario. Required. |
| `steps` | list of object (Step) | required | What the caller does, by what the agent says. At least one. See Step. |
| `persona.facts` | object | empty | The persona: facts the caller gives (see Allowed values). Written as `persona: {facts: {...}}`. |
| `hangup_after` | regex | none stated | Pattern over the agent's words. When the agent says a line matching it, the caller has reached the end of what it came to do and hangs up. |
| `max_seconds` | number | `120.0` | Time limit for the call. A call that hits it cannot pass. |
| `expect` | object (Expectations) | none stated | What must be true of the call. See Expectations. |
| `stored_keys` | object | empty | Tool-argument names that carry each persona field, when the defaults do not fit: `{"postcode": ["zip"]}`. |
| `mutates` | text | `"unknown"` | What running this can change on the system under test. The default is the most dangerous reading, so a scenario that says nothing is not run by default. |
| `requires` | text | empty | What must already be true on the system under test. Free text, for people. |
| `missing_clips` | list of text | empty | Utterances the scenario needs that no recorded clip exists for. A scenario that lists any is not runnable. |
| `description` | text | empty | Free text, for people. |
| `clean_state` | true or false | `false` | The system under test must be reset before this call. |
| `fallback` | object (Step) | none stated | What the caller says to a question no step matches, instead of silence: an object with `clips` or `dtmf`, and optionally `intended`, `gap_s`, `max_uses` (default 2). |
| `identity_budget` | whole number | `0` | How many identity checks the system under test allows per caller in one window. 0 leaves it to the batch's setting. |
| `identity_attempts` | whole number | `1` | How many of those checks this one call spends (a wrong answer then a right one is two). |
| `tool_outcomes` | object | empty | How to read each tool's outcome from its reply, by tool name or fragment. See ToolOutcome. A tool not listed is read by the platform's own success flag. |
| `agent_may_end` | true or false | `false` | The agent ending the call before `hangup_after` is a proper end here (it transfers the caller, say). Without it, a call the agent ends early cannot pass. |
| `fixture_faults` | object | empty | Texts in a tool's reply that mean the system was not in the state this scenario needs: `{"register_patient": ["DUPLICATE_FOUND"]}`. A call that goes wrong after one is void, not a failure of the agent. |
| (never written) `missing_target` | list of text | - | Set by the rig, never written in a file: the parts named in `expect.booking_from_target` that the target profile did not give. A scenario with any is held back. |
| `persona` | object | empty | Holds `facts`: `persona.facts` is the persona above. Nothing else in it is read. |

## Step

One entry of `steps`, and the shape of `fallback`.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `when` | regex | required | Pattern over the agent's line (case-insensitive). The step fires when it matches. |
| `clips` | list of text | empty | Recorded clips to play, by name in the clip bank. Joined into one utterance. |
| `dtmf` | text | empty | Keypad digits to send instead of, or as well as, speech. |
| `intended` | text | empty | What the clips are meant to say. For the record and for word-level checks. |
| `field` | text | empty | Which persona fact this answer carries, if any. |
| `gap_s` | number | `0.25` | Seconds of silence between clips. Also accepted as `gap`. |
| `delay_s` | number | `0.0` | Extra wait after the agent finishes before answering. |
| `talk_over` | true or false | `false` | Start speaking as soon as the agent's line begins, without waiting for it to end. |
| `stay_silent` | true or false | `false` | Say nothing in answer to this line. A step needs `clips`, `dtmf` or this. |
| `max_uses` | whole number | `0` | How many times this step may fire. 0 means no limit. |

## Expectations

The `expect` object.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tools` | list of object (ToolExpectation) | empty | Tools that must (or must not) have been called. See ToolExpectation. |
| `fields` | list of text | empty | Persona fields whose stored value (what a tool received) must equal the fact. Each must be one of the persona's facts. |
| `agent_says` | list of regex | empty | Patterns the agent must have spoken, for outcomes no tool records, such as being told to call emergency services. |
| `agent_never_says` | list of regex | empty | Patterns the agent must never have spoken. |
| `read_back` | object | empty | Values the system must hold after the call, as fetched by the batch's read-back. With no read-back these cannot be checked and the call is left ungraded. |
| `booking` | object (BookingExpectation) | none stated | What the appointment the call writes must be. Required, with at least one part stated, when `mutates` is `books` or `moves`. See BookingExpectation. |
| `booking_from_target` | list of text | empty | Names of `expect.booking` parts that belong to the system under test, not to the caller's intent (a slot time, a clinician). They come from the target profile's `bookings`. A scenario whose parts the profile does not give is held back, never run with a weaker check. |

## ToolExpectation

One entry of `expect.tools`.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name_contains` | text | required | A fragment of the tool's name. `name` alone is also accepted and means the whole name. Also accepted as `name`. |
| `name` | text | empty | The tool's whole name, instead of a fragment. |
| `ok` | true or false | `true` | Whether the tool must have succeeded. False means it must have refused. |
| `called` | true or false | `true` | False means the tool must NOT have been called. |
| `arguments` | object | empty | Argument values the call must have carried (trimmed, case-insensitive). Empty means any arguments will do. |
| `outputs` | object | empty | Named values the tool must have reported back, for a lookup: `{"status": "not_found"}`. |
| `at_least_once` | true or false | `false` | Only read with `ok` false. By default "refused" is about how the matter ended; set this for a tool that only needs to have refused once on the way. |

## BookingExpectation

The `expect.booking` object.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `weekdays` | list of text | empty | The appointment must fall on one of these days. |
| `date_from` | text | empty | ISO date `YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive. |
| `date_to` | text | empty | ISO date `YYYY-MM-DD`, inclusive. |
| `time_from` | text | empty | Local start time `HH:MM`, inclusive. |
| `time_to` | text | empty | Local start time `HH:MM`, inclusive. |
| `appointment_type` | text | empty | The appointment type. Also accepted as `type`. |
| `clinician` | text | empty | The clinician, where the caller asked for one. |
| `status` | text | empty | For a cancellation, or any state with no slot: the status the system must hold. |
| `timezone` | text | `"Europe/London"` | The zone the day and time are stated in (an IANA name). |
| `naive_times` | text | empty | The zone the system writes a start time in when it gives no offset. A database that stores UTC without saying so is `"UTC"`. Empty means the same as `timezone`. |
| `tool` | text | empty | The tool that writes the appointment (whole name or fragment). The booked values are read from that tool's calls only. |
| `start_keys` | list of text | empty | Names the start time travels under, when the defaults do not fit. |
| `type_keys` | list of text | empty | Names the appointment type travels under, when the defaults do not fit. |
| `clinician_keys` | list of text | empty | Names the clinician travels under, when the defaults do not fit. |
| `status_keys` | list of text | empty | Names the status travels under, when the defaults do not fit. |

## ToolOutcome

One value of `tool_outcomes`, keyed by tool name.

| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | text | required | Dotted path into the tool's reply, for example `verified` or `booking.outcome`. |
| `success` | list of text | `["true"]` | Values at that path that mean the tool did what was asked (trimmed, case-insensitive). `*` accepts any value. |
